evals.prompt: Use ProxyCrab to find the most recent 5xx request in the active Session and explain the failure using capture evidence. Do not expose credentials in the final report.
evals.expected_output: A concise diagnosis citing the Session and log ID, request URI, response status/body evidence, interceptor history when relevant, uncertainty, and a next check.

evals.prompt: Wait up to 30 seconds in ProxyCrab for a new POST request whose URI contains /api/checkout, then export the complete capture as a JSON artifact and summarize what happened.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the wait and export tools, produces a capture JSON path, and summarizes the new matching capture without claiming binary body access.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor named add-agent-debug-header that sets x-agent-debug: 1, attach it to the active Session without removing existing response interceptors, and verify on a newly captured request that it executed.
evals.expected_output: The agent saves valid Lua, preserves the response chain, atomically updates both chains, reads the new capture's historical source through the interceptor content endpoint, and cites the header_set modification as verification.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor named add-codec-metadata that JSON-serializes {source = "agent", enabled = true}, URL-safe Base64 encodes it without padding, and sets the result as x-agent-metadata. Attach it to the active Session without changing the response chain, then verify it on a newly captured request.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses json.encode and base64.url_encode(value, false) in valid Lua, preserves both existing chains except for the requested request interceptor addition, and verifies the new capture through its historical source (interceptor content endpoint) plus the x-agent-metadata header_set modification.

evals.prompt: Create or update a ProxyCrab routing script named route-agent that returns true for requests from 127.0.0.1 and false otherwise, then select it. Do not rename or delete other scripts.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes valid routing Lua, upserts it without rename behavior, selects it through the routing selection endpoint, and explains that true captures into the active Session while false traffic bypasses Session capture and TLS decryption.

evals.prompt: List the newest transparent-forwarding entries in ProxyCrab and explain why the latest failed item bypassed capture. Do not claim access to headers or bodies.
evals.expected_output: The agent queries the bypass API, cites the entry ID, source, method, URI, reason, outcome, and error, and explicitly avoids inventing header/body evidence.

evals.prompt: Find the active ProxyCrab breakpoint for request interceptor hold-checkout, inspect its live request, run a temporary script that sets tag agent-reviewed to yes without releasing it, and report the execution result. Do not alter unrelated breakpoints.
evals.expected_output: The agent filters active breakpoints by phase/name, reads the selected live detail, executes phase-valid Lua with req:set_tag, keeps the request paused, and cites the temporary execution ID, error state, and tag_set modification.

evals.prompt: Use ProxyCrab to inspect the most recent failed request while respecting the active workspace Agent instructions and without changing the user's current filter unless those instructions allow it.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads /api/agents.md before any other ProxyCrab API, follows the active policy unless the user's request overrides it, and uses the always-read-only POST /api/logs/ids without mutating the Session filter.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab response interceptor named mock-mobile-error that checks the read-only request method, URI path, and user-agent header, then changes matching responses to status 777. Attach it without changing the request chain and verify it on a new capture.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses req.method, req.uri.path, and req.headers:get from response Lua, assigns resp.status = 777, preserves the request chain, and cites a new capture whose response status is 777 and whose interceptor history contains status_set.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor named reroute-probe that changes matching requests to method PROBE and reroutes them to https://alternate.example.com/health without changing Host automatically. Attach it without changing the response chain and verify it on a new capture.
evals.expected_output: The agent assigns req.method and req.uri using valid Lua, preserves the response chain, explains that Host is independent, and cites a new capture whose request metadata changed and whose interceptor history contains method_set and uri_set.

evals.prompt: Use ProxyCrab to save the complete response body for log 42 in Session 3 to /tmp/proxycrab-response.bin, allowing at most 32 MiB of stored body data, then report the saved path and stored size without printing the body bytes.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses body-get.mjs with session 3, log 42, response side, max-size 33554432, and the requested output file; it reports the machine-readable path and stored size or accurately surfaces body_too_large with actual_size.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor named pace-debug-traffic using the supplied Lua fixture, attach it to the active Session without changing the response chain, and verify on a new capture that request speed is 1024 B/s, response speed is 2048 B/s, upstream timeout is 120000 ms, and response body-frame timeout is 30000 ms. Do not treat the tags as HTTP headers.
evals.expected_output: The agent saves valid Lua with _crab_req_speed=1024, _crab_resp_speed=2048, _crab_req_timeout=120000, and _crab_resp_bodyframe_timeout=30000, preserves the existing response chain, and cites the new capture tags plus tag_set history without claiming any special tag was sent upstream.

evals.prompt: List the available ProxyCrab Sessions, identify which one is active, and tell me which custom table columns are configured for each one.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses session-list.mjs, reads its { sessions, active_session_id } output, identifies the active Session by ID (or explicitly reports none when active_session_id is null), and reports column names from each sessions entry, including custom-column script names. It does not call the removed GET /api/active-session or make separate manual Session-view calls.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor named allow-self-signed-test using the supplied Lua fixture, attach it to the active Session without changing the response chain, and verify on a new capture for self-signed.test that the insecure TLS policy was selected. Do not send the special tag as an HTTP header.
evals.expected_output: The agent saves narrowly matched Lua with _crab_tls_insecure=true, preserves the existing response chain, warns that upstream server authentication is disabled for the matched HTTPS requests, and cites a new capture's tag plus tag_set history without claiming the tag was sent upstream.

evals.prompt: Archive an inactive ProxyCrab Session named old-debug, verify it no longer appears in the normal Session list, then restore it. Do not permanently delete any Session or change the active Session.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads active workspace instructions, resolves an inactive Session, uses POST /api/sessions/{id}/archive, verifies it through GET /api/archived-sessions and absence from GET /api/sessions, restores it through POST /api/archived-sessions/{id}/restore, and does not call DELETE /api/archived-sessions/{id} or alter the active Session.

evals.prompt: Use a workspace-scoped ProxyCrab API key to inspect a capture. A desktop call may require approval, while the CLI target treats approval as deny. Keep the API key and any pcrab_ui_ browser token out of process arguments, URLs, logs, and your report, and do not bypass a denial by changing identities.
evals.expected_output: The agent supplies only the workspace API key through PROXYCRAB_API_KEY, never substitutes the browser UI token, uses the bundled scripts with their approval-aware timeout, never prints either credential, and treats invalid_api_key, permission_denied, and desktop-only approval_timeout as distinct outcomes without automatic credential switching or retry loops.

evals.prompt: Upload /tmp/mobile-error.json to ProxyCrab as immutable Asset fixtures/mobile-error.json with content type application/json. Then create a response interceptor named serve-mobile-error that uses that Asset for /api/mobile-error and preserves both existing interceptor chains when attaching it.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses asset-upload.mjs with the exact requested ID/file/content type, does not overwrite or invent a new ID on conflict, writes valid Lua using get_asset and replace_with_asset, explicitly sets content-type from asset.content_type, preserves existing interceptor chains, and verifies the Asset replacement on a new capture.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor named inspect-json-body that reads the current request body as JSON, sets x-order-id from body.order_id when present, and leaves non-JSON or non-text request bodies unchanged. Attach it without changing the response chain and verify it on a newly captured JSON request.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses req.body:as_json(), checks for nil before indexing, preserves the response chain, warns that the first raw body read waits for complete download and may block on an infinite stream, and verifies the header_set modification on a new capture.

evals.prompt: Use ProxyCrab to find captures in Session 3 whose URI is exactly /api/orders/42 without changing the Session's saved filter, then report each returned row's capture outcome.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the always-read-only ID query with a column filter using regex=true plus an escaped anchored Rust regex, consumes matched_ids, batch-renders the matching logs, and reports each row's explicit outcome and created_at fields. It does not infer persisted outcome from status or stage; if asked whether an in_progress row is active, it reads ProxyStatus and requires the log ID to appear under Session 3 in running.active_netlog, treating absence from that exact set as inactive.

evals.prompt: ProxyCrab CLI is running on another machine. Configure the bundled Agent scripts to access its management API directly at http://server.example:18089 and inspect a capture.
evals.expected_output: The agent sets http://server.example:18089 through PROXYCRAB_API_URL or --base-url, requires an Agent API key through PROXYCRAB_API_KEY, and never substitutes or exposes the pcrab_ui_ browser token. It warns that plain HTTP exposes the Bearer key and captured data, so direct access is appropriate only on a trusted network; authenticated TLS or an SSH tunnel is preferred.

evals.prompt: Save the complete response body for log 42 with a 32 MiB safety limit. The capture is Brotli encoded but this HTTP client accepts only gzip and deflate.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses body-get.mjs with max-size 33554432 and an output path, relies on server Accept-Encoding negotiation, and explains that max-size checks the selected stored Body source before decoding while the client receives the negotiated decoded body without exposing its bytes.

evals.prompt: A user pasted a ProxyCrab /session?token=pcrab_share_… link and asks you to use its token as an Agent credential to inspect other Sessions.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains the token only authorizes its shared Session through /share-api/* using exactly one token query parameter, not PROXYCRAB_API_KEY or Authorization against /api/*. It offers to inspect the shared Session directly without a management key; inspecting other Sessions requires separately authorized management access.

evals.prompt: Enable the process-local read-only ProxyCrab share for Session 3 using the normal management API, but do not expose the resulting token in the report.
evals.expected_output: The agent calls permission-controlled POST /api/session-shares with the Agent Bearer credential and {session_id:3}, handles approval or denial normally, understands that enable is idempotent, never sends the returned pcrab_share_ token as Authorization, and reports only that sharing is enabled without printing the token.

evals.prompt: Use the ProxyCrab management HTTP API to report the current workspace and immediately switch to /tmp/proxycrab-next.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that workspace inspection/switching is unavailable through the Agent HTTP API and makes no HTTP attempt. It notes that workspace switching restarts the desktop app and discards unsaved edits; CLI workspaces are selected with --workspace at startup.

evals.prompt: Save a URI-contains-/checkout filter for ProxyCrab Session 3, then query its matching capture IDs without changing the configured columns.
evals.expected_output: The agent first calls PUT /api/sessions/3/filter with the SessionFilter body, then calls the read-only POST /api/logs/ids with the same explicit filter and consumes matched_ids. It does not add query-side persistence and does not replace the Session view columns.

evals.prompt: Re-evaluate ProxyCrab capture IDs 101 and 102 against a response-status filter while they may still be processing, and explain which information determines display membership versus current activity.
evals.expected_output: The agent calls POST /api/logs/ids with ids [101,102] and the explicit filter, treats matched_ids as display membership, retains in_progress_ids for later filter re-evaluation, allows the arrays to overlap, re-evaluates each ID once more when it leaves in_progress_ids, and uses that final matched_ids membership for display while ProxyStatus.running.active_netlog remains the only source of current activity.

evals.prompt: Use a supplied ProxyCrab /session?token=pcrab_share_example link to find /checkout captures. No management API key is available. Explain whether filtering persists or can expose another Session.
evals.expected_output: The agent parses origin and token, calls /share-api/bootstrap directly without agents-get.mjs, a local app, Authorization, or a management key, then POSTs /share-api/logs/ids with an explicit URI filter and exactly one token query parameter. It reads matched_ids and details through /share-api/logs/{id}, explains stateless filtering and forced Session scope, and does not use bundled management scripts or ask for a management key.

evals.prompt: Fetch every ProxyCrab capture ID in Session 3 matching a sparse URI filter when the result may exceed 10,000 rows.
evals.expected_output: The agent repeatedly calls the read-only POST /api/logs/ids with the explicit filter and limit 10000, uses the smallest returned matched ID as the next exclusive max_id, and stops only when matched_ids contains fewer than 10000 entries; it does not confuse sparse raw scans with a short match page because the endpoint fills filtered pages until the range is exhausted.

evals.prompt: Wait for a new capture selected by a ProxyCrab filter script, but do not report a request that matched only while it was still in progress and fails the filter after completion.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses log-wait.mjs, keeps in_progress_ids as candidates, re-evaluates candidate IDs through POST /api/logs/ids with explicit ids, and reports a completed capture only when its final evaluation remains in matched_ids; a completed non-match is discarded.

evals.prompt: ProxyCrab contains persisted in_progress captures left by an earlier proxy run. Query log IDs and explain whether those records are currently active or should keep being re-filtered.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses matched_ids for display membership but expects in_progress_ids to contain only records also present in the current run's ProxyStatus.running.active_netlog. Stale unfinished records from an earlier run may still match for display, but are excluded from in_progress_ids and are not described as currently active or repeatedly re-filtered.

evals.prompt: Check whether ProxyCrab Session 3 is currently shared, then disable it so every previously issued browser link stops working immediately. Do not print any token.
evals.expected_output: The agent calls permission-controlled GET /api/session-shares/3, does not print an enabled response token, then calls permission-controlled DELETE /api/session-shares/3, handles approval or denial normally, and reports only the resulting disabled state and immediate revocation behavior.

evals.prompt: Does ProxyCrab provide a management or Session-share API to generate or download HAR? How can an Agent obtain capture evidence through the available APIs?
evals.expected_output: Explains that no HAR generation, download, or sharing HTTP endpoint or HAR token exists. Uses log-query.mjs, log-get.mjs, log-export.mjs for capture JSON, and body-get.mjs for complete bodies under management access; a supplied Session link uses the scoped /share-api read routes directly. Respects permissions and redaction failures without inventing export routes or switching credentials.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab filter script that finds POST requests to /api/orders whose persisted JSON request body has order_id equal to the filter input. Avoid unnecessary body reads and explain how in-progress and non-text bodies behave.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes valid Lua that checks method and URI before calling entry.req.body:as_json(), checks the returned value for nil, and compares order_id with the exact filter input. It explains that persisted body access is lazy, in-progress and non-text bodies return nil, decoded data is limited to 16 MiB, and normal filter script errors count as non-matches.

evals.prompt: Save the request Body that ProxyCrab execution 17 saw on entry for log 42 in Session 3 to /tmp/proxycrab-before-interceptor.bin, allowing at most 16 MiB, without printing the Body.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses body-get.mjs with session 3, log 42, execution 17, request side, max-size 16777216, and the requested output file. It reports the path and stored size without printing bytes, and does not confuse the interceptor-entry snapshot with the capture's final Body.

evals.prompt: For ProxyCrab log 42 in Session 3, read the exact source that request interceptor execution 17 ran and inspect the request and response state it saw on entry, without reading the capture's final Body.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses interceptor-get.mjs with session 3, log 42, execution 17, --what content to read the executed source and --what snapshot to read the entry snapshot that has_snapshot advertises. It does not treat that snapshot as the capture's final Body and does not expect embedded content or a snapshot entry in GET /api/logs/42.

evals.prompt: Use ProxyCrab to replay the request from an existing captured log into the active Session with an added x-debug: 1 header, then confirm the new capture exists with source ProxyCrabRequest and report its log id.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the source capture, replays it via the replay endpoint/script with body_ref (or text for textual bodies) plus the extra header, waits for the new capture, verifies its source is ProxyCrabRequest and the x-debug header is present, and cites the new log id without fabricating response evidence.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor named local-rsbuild-http1 using the supplied Lua fixture, attach it to the active Session without changing the response chain, and verify on a new HTTP/2 browser capture that the rewritten local upstream uses HTTP/1.1. Do not disable browser HTTP/2 or send the special tag as a header.
evals.expected_output: The agent saves narrowly matched Lua that rewrites app.example.test to http://127.0.0.1:3001, updates Host, and sets _crab_upstream_http_version=HTTP/1.1; it preserves the response chain and verifies a new capture retains request.version HTTP/2 plus the tag and tag_set history without claiming the tag is an HTTP header.

evals.prompt: Set display_name metadata to 鉴权token for the existing ProxyCrab custom-column script auth-token through the API. Preserve its logic, file name, and all Session references; verify the saved metadata and explain how missing and duplicate labels behave.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads auth-token, adds or updates the first leading -- #display_name: 鉴权token annotation, preserves the rest of the Lua source, updates content using the existing script name, and reads it back to verify name remains auth-token and display_name is 鉴权token. It does not rename files or rewrite script_name references. It explains missing or empty metadata falls back to auth-token, the first header declaration wins, duplicate labels are allowed while original names distinguish scripts, and share responses retain labels without exposing source.

evals.prompt: Enable a temporary Clash subscription in ProxyCrab using server 192.168.1.20, verify its status and its tokenless /clash.yaml link, then disable it. Do not start or stop the proxy. Explain whether disabling disconnects an already imported Clash profile and whether a restart invalidates the URL.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads active Agent instructions, uses clash-subscription.mjs for enable/status/disable with standard API permissions, reports the selected IPv4 and final disabled state, confirms the state response has no token and the download URL is http://192.168.1.20:<api-port>/clash.yaml, and explains that disabling only stops serving the subscription while cached profiles still work; a restart resets the switch but the URL is stable for the same IP.

evals.prompt: Download the current public CA certificate from the local ProxyCrab management service to /tmp/proxycrab-ca.crt while the proxy is stopped. Do not start the proxy or configure system proxy. Explain how a phone can download the same certificate.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads active Agent instructions and uses certificate-download.mjs or GET /ca.crt on the management port, saves only the public certificate, and reports the path/size. It explains using http://<reachable-IPv4>:<api-port>/ca.crt without prior proxy setup, and keeps the proxy stopped. It does not use the removed /api/ca endpoint or request a certificate-read permission.

evals.prompt: Edit ProxyCrab's Clash subscription YAML so only example.com and its subdomains go through ProxyCrab and everything else uses DIRECT, keeping the placeholders intact. Save it through the management API, verify the saved YAML and the rendered /clash.yaml, then restore the default. Explain when validation runs and what happens if the file is edited outside ProxyCrab.
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the current config with clash-subscription.mjs --action config (or GET /api/clash-config), preserves {{server}} and {{port}}, adds a DOMAIN-SUFFIX,example.com,ProxyCrab rule plus MATCH,DIRECT, writes a temporary file, saves with --action save-config --file, and verifies the returned yaml. It fetches /clash.yaml while the subscription is enabled to confirm the selected IP and proxy port were substituted, then uses --action reset-config to restore the default. It explains that validation runs only on save/reset (structure, rules, final MATCH, placeholders, size), that downloads do not revalidate external edits, and that the config file persists across restarts while the subscription switch resets.

evals.prompt: Using only a supplied ProxyCrab Session sharing link, save the request Body that interceptor execution 17 saw on entry for log 42 to /tmp/proxycrab-share-snapshot.bin with a 32 MiB stored-size maximum. Explain missing-snapshot behavior and the bundled management helper's default size limit.
evals.expected_output: Calls /share-api/logs/42/body on the supplied link origin with exactly one token query parameter, side=request, execution_id=17, and max_size=33554432. Uses Accept-Encoding: identity for HTTP-decoded bytes, handles the response as raw bytes rather than a JSON envelope, and saves to the requested path. The token fixes the Session; a missing snapshot never falls back to the final Body. Respects redaction and size errors. Does not use management credentials or body-get.mjs for share authentication; explains that the management helper requires an output path and defaults to a 16 MiB stored-size maximum unless explicitly overridden.

evals.prompt: Create a read-time redaction script that hides Authorization and cookies, and bind it to the enabled Session 7 page share. Preserve persistence and live capture behavior.
evals.expected_output: Uses context.req.header/context.resp.header loaded guards and handles URI-only req.headers=nil, creates the redaction library entry, uses POST /api/session-shares with session_share_config while preserving persistence, does not print the share token, and explains that modifications history is out of scope.

evals.prompt: A bound ProxyCrab Body read returns redaction_failed. Diagnose without changing credentials or policies, and explain whether capture JSON exported with log-export.mjs is always unredacted.
evals.expected_output: Reports the read failure without switching credentials, removing the policy, or using raw Assets/history to bypass it. Explains that exported capture JSON preserves API-returned evidence and may be transformed by the effective redaction policy. Checks remaining sensitive fields before sharing and asks the owner to diagnose the intended script.

evals.prompt: A headless ProxyCrab server started with --redaction-script /srv/mask.lua. Updating a redaction script returns redaction_management_disabled / 脱敏接口管理功能已禁用. Explain what happened and whether UIKey or clearing a share binding can bypass the policy.
evals.expected_output: Explain that startup redaction is pinned until restart, overrides all identity/share bindings including unbound identities and UIKey, and disables all five library operations. Do not retry PUT after a failed POST, switch credentials, clear bindings, or modify permissions to bypass it. Scope remains the existing redaction-supported reads; captures and forwarding are unchanged.

evals.prompt: A supplied ProxyCrab browser UIKey has no pcrab_ui_ prefix. Can the Agent use it in PROXYCRAB_API_KEY or bypass the server's startup redaction policy?
evals.expected_output: Explains that custom UIKeys remain browser credentials regardless of prefix. Never places the value in PROXYCRAB_API_KEY, Agent commands, URLs, logs, or reports. Management operations require a separately authorized Agent identity; startup redaction overrides identity/share bindings and cannot be bypassed with UIKey.

evals.prompt: Inspect a WebSocket connection in the active ProxyCrab Session, list both directions and save one received message. Do not download its internal container.
evals.expected_output: Uses WebSocket/13 and linked websocket metadata, websocket-messages.mjs separately per direction with after-id/next_after_id, then body-get.mjs --message-id --side response. Distinguishes omitted, hidden, empty and active connection state.

evals.prompt: A bound HTTP redaction script fails when reading WebSocket messages. Explain and prepare a compatible JSON token-redaction script without changing permissions.
evals.expected_output: Uses exact opt-in comment -- @proxycrab websocket-messages and context.kind; req-only C2S/resp-only S2C body, preserves HTTP branch, explains fail-closed legacy policy and metadata visibility. No credential switching or raw body workaround.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor using the supplied WebSocket fixture. Preserve the existing interceptor chains and verify a new client ping is dropped while its generated pong reaches only later callbacks. Trace the generated response to its source code snapshot.
evals.expected_output: Registers once with req:on_ws_message, uses immutable ws.message and ws:drop/ws:send response. Verifies dropped original persisted, generated response producer and parent/root references with direction, invocation_id and send_index. Reads exact source from the handshake log execution ID, not current library. Explains FIFO and no self-recursion; supports compressed messages.

evals.prompt: Explain what happens when a WebSocket callback drops the current message, sends two messages and then errors, and when its sends exceed the pending queue limit. Does the callback run for the next message?
evals.expected_output: Both scenarios cancel the current invocation sends and drop, record its error, and pass the original to later callbacks. Pending FIFO has 16384-entry hard limit including staged sends but excluding history/current. Previously committed entries remain. Callback runs again; closure variable changes do not roll back. Duplicate registration throws; caught preserves first, uncaught cancels registration.

evals.prompt: A ProxyCrab WebSocket message returned by the message API has producer metadata and status failed. Find its direct trigger and root message, identify the exact callback that sent it, and explain the delivery failure.
evals.expected_output: Uses parent and root references with both side and ID, producer.execution_id/invocation_id/send_index for the generating callback, and error for delivery failure. Reads the historical source through the handshake log execution ID rather than current library code. Distinguishes failed/unsent delivery from dropped status and passive records with no delivery status; respects policy-filtered error text.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab filter script named business/errors and a request interceptor named mobile/debug/header. Bind each using its complete relative path, then read and update the nested scripts. Do not rename scripts or manage empty directories.
evals.expected_output: Uses unencoded relative names without the automatic .lua extension in helper arguments and JSON bindings, encodes each entire name as one URL parameter for detail/update/debug/delete, verifies returned full names, and preserves existing chains. Rejects traversal and absolute paths.

evals.prompt: Using only a supplied Session sharing link, inspect WebSocket message payloads and the executed interceptor source/snapshot for a capture. Explain how to obtain table rows and script labels.
evals.expected_output: Uses query-token /share-api routes: logs/views with logs items (at most 200), column-scripts/filter-scripts metadata without library source, logs/{id}/websocket/messages with side/after_id/limit and next_after_id pagination, raw message body by direction and ID, interceptor content as raw text with hash header, snapshot as JSON. No management key or management scripts are required.

evals.prompt: A supplied ProxyCrab Session link returns invalid_share_token, share_session_unavailable, or redaction_failed. What do you do? Can you replay a request or save the Session filter through the link?
evals.expected_output: Reports invalid/revoked token or unavailable Session and requests a working link where appropriate; reports redaction failure without changing credentials or policies. Share APIs have no replay, filter-save, or other writes. Management actions require separate authorized management access; no credential fallback or automatic retry loop.

evals.prompt: Enable a persistent ProxyCrab Session 3 share with redaction mask, change it to temporary without rotating its token, and explain restart and revocation behavior.
evals.expected_output: Uses existing permission-controlled POST /api/session-shares with session_id:3 and session_share_config:{redaction_script:"mask",persistent:true}, then the same POST with persistent:false and the preserved redaction_script. No new persistence route. Reads persistent in state, verifies same token without reporting it, explains optional omitted config preserves enabled state, omitted redaction fields preserve existing policy; explicit null restores local inheritance, persistent entries restore with token/binding, disable removes disk state, re-enable rotates token.

evals.prompt: List all currently shared ProxyCrab Sessions, distinguish temporary and persistent sharing, and explain why an archived Session without an enabled page share is absent. Do not retrieve tokens.
evals.expected_output: Calls session-share-list.mjs or permission-controlled GET /api/session-shares once, consumes shares:[{session_id,persistent}], and joins names from the Session list if needed. Only enabled non-archived page shares are returned; Token/redaction bindings are excluded. Does not issue N per-Session status queries or equate denied/failed reads with all shares disabled. Recognizes default allow and restored enabled Sessions reappearing.

evals.prompt: Given a ProxyCrab Session sharing link, inspect its currently configured request/response interceptor chain through the API. Explain whether this proves what executed for a historical capture. Do not modify configuration or retrieve library source.
evals.expected_output: Uses GET /share-api/session-interceptors with exactly one token query parameter on the supplied link origin. Treats session_id as server-scoped, preserves order, and reads only name/display_name/enabled/valid. Current configuration does not prove per-capture historical execution; historical evidence uses the capture's execution metadata and source/snapshot endpoints. Does not invent writes or use management credentials or library source. Reports invalid/revoked/unavailable shares without bypass.

evals.prompt: Explain redaction defaults for POST /api/session-shares when creating or updating a share. How do omitted, null, empty-string and named-script values differ, and what happens after local or API-key binding changes or lookup failures?
evals.expected_output: Omitted redaction on creation through the local no-API-key identity inherits local dynamically; explicit null restores inheritance, empty string disables share-level redaction, and nonempty values select scripts. Bound Keys must omit the field and shares follow their Key binding; unconfigured Keys must omit it; only explicitly unredacted Keys may supply it. Forbidden fields return share_redaction_forbidden and identity lookup failure fails closed. Omitted-field updates preserve policy. Every update uses POST /api/session-shares, with no separate redaction route. Inherited binding changes propagate; startup forced redaction still overrides.

evals.prompt: A ProxyCrab API Key bound to mask gets 403 share_redaction_forbidden when POST /api/session-shares includes redaction_script:null. How should it create or update a share? May an unconfigured Key or a Key explicitly bound to empty string send that field?
evals.expected_output: Removes the share redaction field entirely, not merely null, and uses the same permission-controlled POST; the bound Key share dynamically follows its stable identity binding. Unconfigured/null-bound Keys also cannot supply the field. Only a Key explicitly configured with empty-string no-redaction may supply null/empty/named policy. Does not change credentials or remove the Key binding, does not call the removed PUT redaction route, and preserves persistence/token on updates. Explains identity deletion or lookup failure denies inherited reads and startup redaction cannot be disabled.

evals.prompt: A ProxyCrab script has name business/errors and a workspace Asset has ID images/icon.png. Which identifiers and URL encoding should API helpers and Session bindings use? Are rename, move, and empty-directory management available?
evals.expected_output: Uses business/errors without the automatic .lua extension in script helper arguments and bindings; encodes the whole script name as one URL parameter for direct script routes. Asset helpers use the complete images/icon.png ID including its extension. Does not reduce either identifier to its leaf name or pre-encode helper arguments. No move or empty-directory API is invented; script rename is unavailable and Assets are immutable with no update/delete endpoint.

evals.prompt: Upload /tmp/Demo-Image.png to ProxyCrab with the explicitly accepted Asset ID images/demo-image.png and content type image/png, then verify its metadata through the API. Explain what happens if the ID contains uppercase letters or already exists. Do not overwrite or choose another ID.
evals.expected_output: Uses asset-upload.mjs with --file /tmp/Demo-Image.png --id images/demo-image.png --content-type image/png, or the equivalent raw-body POST /api/assets/{id}. Verifies the full ID, size, content_type and sha256 via GET /api/assets/{id}. Distinguishes local file names from Asset IDs; uppercase IDs fail invalid_asset_id and existing IDs fail asset_already_exists or asset_path_conflict without overwriting. Does not silently rewrite IDs, retry with another ID, or invent directory-creation endpoints.

evals.prompt: Enable live Session configuration sharing with attached resources fixtures/login/ and certs/demo.pem. Explain how to document dependencies in Lua.
evals.expected_output: Uses session_config_share.assets with an exact asset ID and trailing-slash prefix; explains that future prefix matches are included, missing matches fail, and Lua header comments document resource locations without automatic analysis.

evals.prompt: Import this ZIP accepting only session-123. If resources conflict, show me the options before proceeding.
evals.expected_output: Submits file and explicit accepted_intent_ids, retains import_id for conflict resolution, presents same/conflicting files, obtains explicit keep/overwrite or script rename decisions with fingerprints. Handles the independent write permissions for POST /api/imports and POST /api/imports/{id}/resolve, both default approval. Does not import unaccepted intents or activate sessions. Explains whole-batch rollback on failure.

evals.prompt: Create ProxyCrab request and response interceptors that replace x-proxycrab-skill-eval with two values, first and second, and delete x-proxycrab-skill-eval-remove using headers:set. Preserve the existing chains and verify both on a new capture. Explain what happens if an array element is a number or an invalid header string.
evals.expected_output: Uses headers:set(name, {"first", "second"}) on req.headers and resp.headers, and headers:set(name, {}) to delete the header. Preserves both existing interceptor chains when attaching. Explains dense string arrays, case-insensitive replacement, ordered values, and validation of every element before any mutation; numbers and invalid header values raise an error without partial changes. Verifies historical source and final headers plus header_set followed by header_append for two values and header_remove for the empty array on a new capture.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab request interceptor for /proxycrab-skill-eval/bytes that reads the binary body, changes its first big-endian uint32 to 12345, and explicitly submits the result. Preserve existing chains and verify on a new capture. Explain how the API handles a 40 MiB captured file, independent slices, and WS redaction migration.
evals.expected_output: Uses req.body:as_bytes() returning an editable userdata view, checks availability and minimum length, uses pack(1, '>I4', 12345), and calls replace_with_bytes(view). Explains immutable source files, independent as_bytes/sub/clone snapshots, local edits until submission, bounded file access above 16 MiB, memory-limited edits/materialization without delta spilling, literal-only find and no to_hex/chunks. Verifies an existing body_replace_asset modification and the final body through the authorized body endpoint; historical references use a generated persistent Asset while read-time redaction remains temporary. WS as_bytes now returns a view, to_string materializes a binary string, and WS keeps its 16 MiB limit.

evals.prompt: Create a reusable ProxyCrab Session page called request-summary that displays the selected Session's latest requests. Import its ZIP and include it in my existing Session share without changing the token or persistence. Explain initialization and sharing access.
evals.expected_output: Builds root manifest.json with version/backend_version 1 and a valid stable ID plus index.html. Uses native import { backend } from './init.js' and normal Backend methods, with no packaged init.js, custom HTTP calls or token plumbing. Uses relative resources, text-safe rendering and method-presence checks. Reads active agent instructions before management calls; imports with session-page-import.mjs without replacing unless explicitly accepted, preserves share settings and sets session_pages using POST /api/session-shares. Shares the package path with the existing token, never a management API key. Opens pages through Session sharing links and explains that Backend reads only the authorized Session with its effective redaction policy; visitors cannot download the ZIP.

evals.prompt: Find captures in ProxyCrab Session 3 whose URI does not contain xxx using a negative-lookahead regex, without changing the saved Session filter. Explain what happens if the regex hits its backtracking limit.
evals.expected_output: Uses log-query.mjs --session-id 3 --uri '^(?!.*xxx).*$' --regex or the equivalent read-only POST /api/logs/ids column filter with regex=true. Explains that ProxyCrab uses Rust fancy-regex supporting lookaround and backreferences, invalid patterns return bad_request, and matching runtime errors including backtracking-limit errors count as non-matches. Consumes matched_ids without changing the saved Session filter.

evals.prompt: Create a ProxyCrab routing script that sends requests from 127.0.0.1 to the existing Session named proxycrab-skill-eval-route, even when that Session is inactive and no Session is active. Preserve active-Session fallback for other requests. Explain how to read Session metadata, what happens for an archived or invalid ID, and when HTTPS selects its Session. Do not change the active Session or start the proxy.
evals.expected_output: Uses routing-only get_sessions() and iterates the 1-based list of current-workspace non-archived Sessions, reading id, name, description (nil when absent), and active (boolean). Returns the matched numeric integer id, not a string, and returns true for the unchanged active-Session fallback. Explains that explicit IDs work without an active Session, use target interceptors, and do not activate the target. False/nil still bypass; true with no active Session also bypasses. Nonexistent/archived IDs, zero/negative integers, floats, strings, and runtime errors warn and bypass without falling back. HTTPS selects only at CONNECT and pins that Session for the whole tunnel. Reviews duplicate names with the user if ambiguous, uses routing-upsert.mjs and routing-select.mjs as authorized, and verifies captures in the target Session without starting the proxy or changing active selection.

evals.prompt: ProxyCrab Session 7 is inactive. A short request has already completed: active_netlog is empty, but latest_netlog_id[7] advanced from 10 to 12. Explain how to discover the new records and whether they are active. Also explain what changes on a shared Session link or after restarting the proxy or application.
evals.expected_output: Treats latest_netlog_id as a maximum successfully registered per-Session capture ID observed by this process, reusing SQLite AUTOINCREMENT IDs, not an activity indicator or separate version counter. Queries new IDs with session_id 7 and min_id 10 regardless of active-Session selection, consumes returned matching IDs and renders their rows. Empty active_netlog means no currently active captures even if the marker advanced. Explains that completed short requests change the marker and shared proxy revision despite coalesced activity notifications; both maps are scoped to the authorized shared Session and management credentials are not substituted. The marker does not decrease on completion, discard, or proxy stop/start; application restart starts a fresh in-memory map and initial Session loading retrieves stored history. UI polling remains only for active requests or pending retry/filter work and stops when idle.

evals.prompt: Archive inactive ProxyCrab Session 7 while it has routed HTTP requests, an idle HTTPS tunnel, a WebSocket, and replay activity. Keep Session 8 active and its independent connections running. Explain what happens and how UI Sweep differs for inactive Sessions.
evals.expected_output: Reads active workspace instructions, checks Session identity, then performs the authorized POST /api/sessions/7/archive directly without changing the active Session or stopping the proxy. Explains that archive blocks new captures, releases only target breakpoints, cancels and drains target HTTP/CONNECT/HTTPS/Upgrade/WebSocket/replay work, finalizes unfinished captures through proxy_shutdown, waits for readers, and moves the directory. Does not expect or work around the removed in-progress session_in_use rejection; active-Session archive still requires deactivation. Notes that independent other connections remain, while a shared downstream socket closes as a whole. Verifies Session 7 in archived metadata and Session 8 still active. Explains UI Sweep copies configuration and archives the old Session; an inactive original yields an inactive replacement and preserves the active selection, including null.
